# Defy

> Defy is the insight and automation platform for agencies that punch above their weight: live competitor, audience and conversation intelligence (Defy Monitor), the ability to interrogate it inside Claude (Defy MCP), and agentic workflows that take the repetitive delivery off your team (Defy Agents) — the same capability the holding networks built for millions, without the build cost or maintenance burden.

Defy (Defy Group Limited) is the insight & automation platform for agencies that punch above their weight. Website: https://defygroup.ai/ · Platform login: https://cloud.defygroup.ai/ · Contact: talktous@defygroup.ai

## Platform
- Defy Monitor: live competitor, audience and conversation intelligence on every client and category.
- Defy MCP: interrogate that data inside Claude — prompt it like a co-worker, no dashboard to learn.
- Defy Agents: agentic workflows that handle repetitive delivery (e.g. reporting), so people focus on the work that wins.

## Who it is for
- Independent agencies (creative, media, CRM, influencer, PR, social) competing with holding-company networks.
- Brands with in-house teams wanting the networks' intelligence stack without agency margin.

## Clients
- SharkNinja (internal strategy team): Defy Monitor to understand LATAM markets and build test-and-learn strategies.
- SAMY (global influencer agency): Defy Agents cut performance reporting from three days to one.
- Enchant (UK CRM agency): Defy Monitor to automate CRM insight and campaign deployment.

## Founders
- Ian Cassidy — CEO & co-founder; 20 years in creative agencies; built and scaled SHARE Creative; private-equity exit to Bridgepoint.
- Alek Farseev — CTO & co-founder; AI professor based in Singapore; leads all technical development.

## Frequently asked questions
### What is Defy?
Defy is an AI insight and automation platform for marketing agencies and in-house brand teams. It combines Defy Monitor (live competitor, audience and conversation intelligence), Defy MCP (interrogate that data inside Claude, no dashboard to learn) and Defy Agents (agentic workflows for repetitive delivery), so independents get the analytical and AI capability of the holding networks without the build cost.

### Who is Defy for?
Independent agencies — creative, media, CRM, influencer, PR and social shops — that compete against holding-company networks, and brands with in-house teams that want direct access to the same intelligence stack without an agency margin layered on top.

### How is Defy different from building our own AI stack?
Building and maintaining an analytics and AI stack takes engineers, data pipelines and constant upkeep. Defy gives you a ready-made stack you can run for every client and category, with insight that traces back to the real published content behind it — without the development cost or the maintenance burden.

### Which brands and agencies use Defy?
SharkNinja's internal strategy team uses Defy Monitor to understand LATAM markets and build test-and-learn strategies. Global influencer agency SAMY uses Defy Agents to streamline performance reporting, cutting three days of work to one. UK CRM agency Enchant uses Defy Monitor to automate CRM insight and campaign deployment for all its clients.

### Who founded Defy?
Defy was founded by Ian Cassidy (CEO), who spent 20 years in creative agencies, built and scaled SHARE Creative and led a nine-figure private-equity exit to Bridgepoint, and Alek Farseev (CTO), an AI professor based in Singapore who leads all of Defy's technical development.

### How do I get started or log in?
Email talktous@defygroup.ai to start a conversation — no pitch. Existing users log in to the Defy platform at cloud.defygroup.ai.

## Journal articles — questions answered (English)
### AI impact on agency jobs: how to rebuild the junior career ladder
URL: https://defygroup.ai/blog/agency-entry-level-talent-ai/
Question: How will AI affect jobs in my agency, including mine, and how do I prepare my team?
Answer: AI is removing task-shaped agency work, not the need for people. Gartner found 18% of senior marketing leaders have cut some roles because of AI, while 16% have created new ones. Reporting, audits and resizing are most exposed. The best preparation is redesigning junior roles around judgement – questioning data, checking AI output and linking insight to outcomes – rather than halting graduate hiring.
Key takeaways:
- Gartner's survey of 1,303 senior marketing leaders found 18% have already eliminated some positions because of AI, 16% have created new roles and nearly a third have reworked existing functions.
- The agency work most exposed to AI is task-shaped – monthly reporting, competitor audits, manual resizing and meeting admin – rather than judgement, taste or client relationships.
- Stopping graduate hiring saves money this year and creates a shortage of experienced account and strategy people in five years' time.
- Juniors whose value was speed at grunt work are prone to imposter feelings when AI takes that work; making critical questioning of data and AI output their explicit job restores confidence.
- The most practical redesign moves juniors from fetching data to interrogating it, with seniors coaching the judgement.

### Outcome-based agency remuneration: the metrics beyond ROAS and CPA
URL: https://defygroup.ai/blog/beyond-roas-cpa-outcome-based-agency-pay/
Question: If clients stop paying for hours, which metrics beyond ROAS and CPA should decide what my agency gets paid?
Answer: Build outcome-based pay on metrics the client's finance team already trusts: incremental revenue measured by marketing mix modelling or holdout tests, contribution margin, new-customer growth and retention. Use ROAS and CPA as diagnostics, not fee triggers, because they are platform-reported and easy to game. Keep a fixed base fee, agree the measurement method upfront and add leading indicators the agency controls.
Key takeaways:
- A WFA and Agency Mania Solutions study of 69 multinationals found labour-based agency pay fell from 54% of remuneration models in 2011 to 17% in 2026.
- ROAS and CPA are useful diagnostics but weak fee triggers, because they are platform-reported, ignore incrementality and can be improved by harvesting demand that already existed.
- The strongest outcome metrics are the ones a client's finance director already reports: incremental revenue, contribution margin, new-customer growth and retention.
- Brands rate briefing, trust and feedback above financial incentives as drivers of agency performance, so outcome pay works best as a way to agree what matters, not as a stick.
- A safe transition keeps a fixed base fee that covers delivery cost, puts a capped share at risk and fixes the measurement method before the work starts.

### How to prove media ROI to clients: why MMM is back and what to show
URL: https://defygroup.ai/blog/proving-media-roi-agencies-mmm/
Question: How can I prove to clients that their media spend is actually driving business results?
Answer: Prove media ROI with layered evidence, not a ROAS screenshot. Use marketing mix modelling to show each channel's incremental contribution and saturation point, validate it with at least one holdout test, and explain why results moved using real audience and competitor evidence. Then present the findings as a reallocation of existing budget, which is easier for a client to approve than a request for more.
Key takeaways:
- Clients increasingly distrust platform-reported ROAS and last-click attribution, because the platform selling the media is also the one measuring it.
- In a case reported by Campaign Middle East, TRKKN's Meridian model of three years of Faces data across 11 channels projected an 8.5% incremental revenue lift from reallocating existing budget.
- Marketing mix modelling shows which channels drive incremental revenue and where spend saturates, but it does not explain why results moved.
- A credible media ROI story combines MMM, at least one controlled experiment and traceable evidence about creative, competitors and audience conversation.
- Presenting ROI findings as a reallocation of existing budget is easier for clients to approve than a request for more spend.

### Marketing dashboard overload: why agencies are swapping logins for questions
URL: https://defygroup.ai/blog/agency-dashboard-fatigue-ai-questions/
Question: How can I simplify all the marketing data I'm looking at so I can make decisions without getting bogged down?
Answer: Start from the decision, not the data. List the handful of decisions you make for each client, write the one question each decision needs answered, and keep only the few metrics that answer it. Then use tools that let you ask that question in plain language and show the evidence behind the answer, instead of logging into another dashboard.
Key takeaways:
- Campaign reported the Ingenuity Pulse finding that only one in three marketers is satisfied with the results of their martech investments, a gap that threatens agency retention.
- Dashboard overload is a cognitive load problem: every extra chart, filter and login uses up the limited attention needed to make a decision.
- The fastest way to simplify marketing data is to start from the decisions you make, then keep only the metrics that answer each decision's question.
- Conversational AI tools can replace many dashboard sessions, but only if every answer can be traced back to the source data.

### Brand differentiation strategy: finding the angle your category ignores
URL: https://defygroup.ai/blog/escape-creative-sameness-category-intelligence/
Question: How do we find a genuinely unique angle so our brand doesn't become invisible in a crowded market?
Answer: Map what your whole category already says before deciding what you will say. Analyse competitors' ads and organic content for their messages, tones, visual codes and the audience tensions they address, then look for relevant tensions nobody owns. Choose the gap that is credible for your brand, brief creatives with the map rather than a template, and commit to it long enough to become familiar.
Key takeaways:
- Sir John Hegarty told Marketing Week that marketing has become 'repetitive, cliché, boring', and that something like 95% of new product launches still fail despite far more data.
- Creative sameness is a herd behaviour problem: under uncertainty, brands and agencies copy what competitors do because it feels safe.
- Category data creates sameness when it is used as a recipe and creates difference when it is used as a map of where everyone else is standing.
- A practical differentiation process audits the whole category's ads and organic content, maps crowded and empty territory, and matches the gaps against real audience tensions.
- Differentiation only pays if the brand commits to it; changing direction too often makes a brand hard to remember.

### AI marketing tools for agencies: build a stack, not a shopping list
URL: https://defygroup.ai/blog/agency-ai-stack-integration/
Question: Which AI marketing tools should my agency use, and how do I make sure they actually work with the systems we already have?
Answer: Choose AI marketing tools by how well they connect, not by their feature lists. Start from the two or three workflows that eat the most hours, map where the data has to flow, and pick tools that share one source of truth, show their working and can be written into client contracts. A connected stack of three beats a dozen clever apps that never talk.
Key takeaways:
- The value of an agency AI stack comes from how its tools connect, not from how many tools it contains.
- Campaign, reporting on the Ingenuity Pulse study, says only one in three marketers is satisfied with the results of their martech investments, a gap that puts agency relationships at risk.
- Digiday reports that agencies are adding AI terms to existing contracts clause by clause, usually when a client wants tool access, asks for AI language or a new AI tool touches their project.
- Before buying another tool, map one workflow end to end and find every point where data is re-keyed, exported or lost.
- Every tool in the stack should be explainable to a client: what it does, what data it touches and how its conclusions can be checked.

### Creative pre-testing: how to end the creativity vs performance war
URL: https://defygroup.ai/blog/creativity-vs-performance-pre-testing/
Question: How do I balance creativity and performance in my campaigns without sanding every idea down to something safe?
Answer: Stop treating them as rivals and move the evidence earlier. Pre-test creative concepts before media spend, using scores as feedback to sharpen ideas rather than as verdicts after the money has gone. That lets bold, human work earn its place with evidence, keeps performance teams confident, and leaves the final call with people who understand the brand.
Key takeaways:
- Creativity and performance clash mainly because performance data usually arrives after the decisions that matter.
- Creative pre-testing scores concepts before media spend, so evidence can improve an idea instead of only judging it.
- Scores shared early with the creative team work as feedback; scores used after launch work as control and push teams towards safe work.
- A clickability score predicts response to an ad, not distinctiveness or long-term brand building, so craft judgement still decides.
- Agreeing in advance to protect one bold route that scores acceptably stops pre-testing from rewarding only the safest idea.

### The agency sprint model: how to move fast without breaking strategy
URL: https://defygroup.ai/blog/agency-sprint-model-speed-strategy/
Question: How can my agency adapt strategy quickly enough to keep up with digital advertising, without the work getting sloppy?
Answer: Work in short, fixed sprints, but keep strategy outside the sprint. Decide the few things that must not change for a quarter, run tactics in sprints of days or weeks, and automate the monitoring, reporting and competitor checks that usually get skipped when time is tight. Speed comes from removing chores, not from removing rigour.
Key takeaways:
- The agency sprint model sells fixed, short engagements measured in days or weeks instead of retainers or months-long projects.
- Campaign US reports that X&O's sprints average three to four weeks and that clients return several times a year instead of signing agency-of-record contracts.
- The main risk of sprints is unconnected work: sharp tactics with no strategy holding them together.
- A one-page strategy spine that lasts a quarter lets sprints move quickly on tactics without rewriting the strategy each time.
- Automating monitoring, reporting and resizing protects rigour, because the checks that usually get skipped are produced without anyone having to find the time.

### Synthetic audiences are taking off. Here's how agencies keep them honest
URL: https://defygroup.ai/blog/synthetic-audiences-agencies-validation/
Question: Are synthetic audiences a reliable source of audience insight, and how do I know when to trust them?
Answer: Synthetic audiences are reliable for speed, hypotheses and scenario testing, not as a substitute for real people. Treat every synthetic finding as a hypothesis, check it against observed behaviour such as what audiences actually publish and discuss, and validate the important ones with a small live test. If a conclusion can't be traced to real evidence, keep it out of the client deck.
Key takeaways:
- Digiday reports that synthetic audiences are moving from experiment into everyday agency planning, with Aveeno Body cutting strategy-brief writing from about 30 days to three.
- Synthetic audiences model people rather than measure them, so they suit hypotheses and scenario testing better than final conclusions.
- Language models tend to return the most common answer, which can hide the minority views and non-obvious tensions agencies are paid to find.
- Fluent, numerical outputs feel more trustworthy than they are, so every synthetic finding should be labelled as synthetic in client work.
- The most reliable approach combines synthetic panels with observed behaviour, such as real published content, and small live tests.

### Agentic AI advertising without the rogue fears: keep humans in the loop
URL: https://defygroup.ai/blog/agentic-media-human-in-the-loop/
Question: How do I use agentic AI in advertising without losing the human connection that builds trust with customers and clients?
Answer: Let agents run the plumbing and keep people on meaning. Agents can plan, pace, optimise and report within limits you set, but humans should approve spend above agreed thresholds, own the message and tone, and plan from real audience conversations. Clear controls reassure clients; human judgement on what the brand says keeps customers' trust.
Key takeaways:
- Agentic AI advertising uses AI agents that plan, buy, optimise and measure with a degree of autonomy, which means they act rather than only suggest.
- Digiday reports that agencies are launching media agents while stressing human oversight, because clients fear rogue agents and hacks.
- Approval thresholds should be set by consequence: routine pacing can run freely, while new audiences, new messages and large budget moves need human sign-off.
- Agents can handle the mechanics of media, but people must own what the brand's message means to its audience.
- Planning from real audience conversations rather than demographic boxes keeps automated optimisation pointed at recognisable human needs.

### Audience research tools: what planners should automate first
URL: https://defygroup.ai/blog/future-of-strategy-planners-automate/
Question: Which audience research tools should I use, and which parts of my strategy work should I automate first?
Answer: Automate the gathering, not the thinking. Planners should hand audience research tools the high-frequency, low-judgement work first: competitor ad audits, social listening round-ups and first-draft personas built from real audience content. Insist that every AI conclusion links back to its source posts. Then reinvest the saved hours in what clients pay strategists for: judgement, sharper questions and the creative leap.
Key takeaways:
- WARC's Future of Strategy 2026 found 56% of strategists see AI replacing strategy roles as their top expected threat, up 15 points, while 66% remain optimistic.
- The first tasks to automate are high-frequency and low-judgement: competitor audits, social listening round-ups and draft personas.
- Desk research is a small market failure inside agencies: unpriced, unmeasured and paid for with senior planners' judgement.
- A good audience research tool shows the real posts behind every conclusion, so the evidence can go in front of a client.
- Automation only produces new thinking if the agency decides in advance where the saved hours will go.

### Influencer marketing reporting: why it's the new agency battleground
URL: https://defygroup.ai/blog/influencer-agency-reporting-automation/
Question: How do I measure ROI on influencer marketing, especially with nano-influencers, so I can allocate budget properly?
Answer: Measure influencer ROI by creator tier, with fully loaded costs that include agency hours, and benchmark cost per qualified engagement or conversion against paid social. Judge nano-influencers on trust signals such as saves, shares and purchase questions rather than likes. Automate data capture and comment classification, but keep the recommendations human and link every claim to the posts behind it.
Key takeaways:
- Influencer reporting has become a competitive weapon: the agency whose reports clients trust is the one that gets the next creator budget.
- Nano-influencer ROI only makes sense with fully loaded costs, tier-specific KPIs and a paid social benchmark.
- Saves, shares and purchase questions in the comments are stronger trust signals than likes or an average engagement rate.
- Automate data capture, comment classification and cost normalisation, but keep the recommendations and the 'so what' human.
- SAMY, a Defy client, used Defy Agents to cut performance reporting from three days of work to one.

### Independent agency vs holding company: how independents compete on data
URL: https://defygroup.ai/blog/independent-agencies-vs-holding-company-data/
Question: As an independent agency, how can I use data as effectively as a holding company, and what data set-up do I actually need?
Answer: Holding companies still lead on scale: proprietary platforms, media buying data and large specialist teams. But as network-grade analytics and AI become available on subscription, independents can match much of that capability without the build or maintenance cost. The deciding factor is shifting from who owns the data stack to who connects data to everyday client decisions fastest.
Key takeaways:
- Holding companies still lead on buying scale and proprietary data, but much of their analytics and AI capability can now be rented by independents.
- Gartner's Jay Wilson told The Drum that agency fees have fallen to 19.2% of marketing budgets and predicts 15% by 2030.
- Omnicom moved at least 468 staff behind its Omni AI platform to Endava, a sign that even the largest groups are rethinking who builds and maintains their technology.
- The digital divide between agencies has shifted from access to tools towards skill in using them and turning that use into outcomes.
- Independents should build data capability around client decisions, not architecture, and rent the category layer rather than build it.

### Agency consolidation or roster? What StarKist and ServiceNow reveal
URL: https://defygroup.ai/blog/agency-consolidation-vs-roster/
Question: Should a brand consolidate its agencies or keep a roster, and what do recent case studies show about which approach works?
Answer: Neither model wins by default. StarKist consolidated with one independent agency, Tombras, for fewer handovers and clearer accountability; ServiceNow chose a team of four Stagwell agencies tied to a technology partnership. In both cases the winning side showed it understood the client well enough to set expectations it could prove. Agencies win big accounts by making their promises measurable.
Key takeaways:
- StarKist consolidated brand strategy, creative, media, social, measurement and SEO assessments with independent agency Tombras, citing limited resources and efficiency.
- Stagwell's three-year ServiceNow partnership is its largest multi-agency deal and includes rolling out ServiceNow's AI platform across Stagwell.
- Expectation Confirmation Theory explains why consolidation is high-stakes: clients judge agencies against what they were promised, not against absolute performance.
- Any agency model can win big accounts, but only if it makes its core promise measurable from the first quarter.
- Pre-testing creative and agreeing one cross-discipline measurement framework are the most practical ways to confirm early expectations.

### Will AI replace marketing agencies? Why the maths rarely adds up
URL: https://defygroup.ai/blog/will-ai-replace-agencies/
Question: Will AI replace my marketing agency, or can it actually help me be more creative and efficient?
Answer: Mostly not. AI replaces agency tasks such as campaign set-up, QA, report assembly and monitoring, but not accountability, relationships or judgement. Once you add the people, tools and management needed to run AI in-house, the saving often disappears. AI does threaten agencies that charge premium fees for admin. Used well, it frees agency teams for more creative, higher-value work.
Key takeaways:
- AI replaces agency tasks, not agency accountability: set-up, QA, reporting and monitoring are the most exposed work.
- Mumbrella's illustrative costing sets a $120,000 retainer against $100,000 to $120,000 for an AI subscription plus one hire, before on-costs and tools.
- Agencies that sell administrative process as expertise are the ones most at risk from AI.
- Clients trust people they can question and hold to account, which is why AI output still needs a named human sign-off.
- AI only makes teams more creative if the hours it saves are ring-fenced for creative and client work in advance.

### Retail media networks and agencies: who really owns the budget?
URL: https://defygroup.ai/blog/retail-media-agency-ownership/
Question: Retail media is growing fast: should it sit with our media agency, a commerce specialist or the performance team?
Answer: Retail media should be owned strategically by whichever agency understands the client's category best, and executed by whoever has the strongest retailer access and tooling. The channel now spans retailer sites, social shops and creator content, so no agency type owns it by default. Independents win the strategy seat with continuous competitor and shopper intelligence, not buying scale.
Key takeaways:
- Retail media now spans retailer sites, social shops and creator content, so no single agency type owns it by default.
- Digiday reports that by June 2026 TikTok Shop was appearing in formal agency RFPs alongside Amazon and Walmart.
- Strategy, execution and measurement of retail media do not need to sit with the same agency, and rosters should say who owns which.
- As AI compresses execution such as bidding, feeds and reporting, agency value moves to understanding the category and challenging the brief.
- Independent agencies can compete without holding-company data deals by keeping a live view of competitors and shopper conversation.

### How to reach Gen Z consumers: plan from communities, not birth years
URL: https://defygroup.ai/blog/gen-z-persona-clustering/
Question: I need strategies that actually reach Gen Z consumers and drive engagement. Where do I start?
Answer: Reach Gen Z by planning from real conversations, not age brackets. Cluster public posts, comments and reviews into personas defined by shared tensions, prove each one with real posts, then reach each cluster through the creators and formats it already chooses to watch. Measure saves, shares and substantive comments alongside reach, and refresh the clusters monthly.
Key takeaways:
- "Gen Z" is a birth-year bracket, and on its own it rarely tells a creative team anything it can brief from.
- Digiday's Media Agency Report 2026 found 75% of respondents say creator marketing has become more important over the past year, with community building the top goal for creator work.
- Persona clusters built from real conversations reveal the tensions, language and objections that demographic segments miss.
- Every AI-generated persona should be traceable to real posts; if it is not, treat it as a hypothesis, not a finding.
- Refresh persona clusters monthly, because online communities move faster than annual segmentation studies.

### AI video production cost: why cheaper frames don't shrink the budget
URL: https://defygroup.ai/blog/ai-video-production-agency-economics/
Question: How much does AI really save on video production, and how do I scale video content without losing quality?
Answer: AI makes each video asset cheaper, mainly in pre-production, versioning, resizing and localisation, but total budgets rarely fall because clients ask for more assets. Shoot costs such as crew, equipment and insurance are still rising in some markets. Agencies protect margin by automating repetitive work, keeping creative and cultural judgement human, and pricing the idea and the system rather than each frame.
Key takeaways:
- AI cuts the cost of individual video assets most in pre-production, versioning, resizing and localisation, not on the shoot.
- Because demand for video assets is price-elastic, cheaper frames usually lead clients to ask for more, not to spend less.
- Pricing per asset hands every AI saving to the client; pricing the idea, the production system and the proof protects margin.
- AI-generated localised content can read as synthetic to local audiences, so cultural sign-off should stay with people from that market.
- Repeat business on integrated, cross-format work is a better health metric for production partners than cost per asset.

### How to optimise marketing budget ROI when global campaigns underdeliver
URL: https://defygroup.ai/blog/global-vs-local-campaign-budget/
Question: How can I optimise my marketing budget so that every pound I spend contributes to a better return?
Answer: Start with creative fit, not media rates. Audit which assets run in each market, read local competitor and audience context, and score creative before buying media. Then move a ring-fenced share of low-confidence spend towards adapted or local work, with pre-agreed rules to scale or stop. Campaign reports new research finding that global campaigns deliver fewer commercial outcomes.
Key takeaways:
- The quickest marketing ROI gains often come from stopping spend behind creative that does not fit its market, not from shaving media rates.
- Campaign reported a study by Publicis London, System1 and Effie which compared global and local-market campaigns and found global campaigns deliver fewer commercial outcomes.
- Prospect theory explains why teams keep the status quo: the risk of change is visible, while the loss from inaction is not.
- Scoring creative before buying media means weak assets are fixed before they absorb budget.
- Pre-agreed rules for scaling or stopping tests take the politics out of reallocating budget.

### Agency pitch strategy: win with a 48-hour category insight sprint
URL: https://defygroup.ai/blog/win-agency-pitches-ai-category-insight/
Question: A brief has just landed. Which market research tools and pitch strategy will give us a real insight before the deadline?
Answer: Lead with the client's category, not your credentials. In the 48 hours after a brief lands, map competitors' paid and organic content, cluster the audience conversation into personas and tensions, and find the angle no competitor has claimed. Trace every claim to real ads and posts. An insight-led pitch gives the client a view it cannot compare on price.
Key takeaways:
- The strongest agency pitch strategy leads with the client's competitive position, not the agency's credentials.
- Digiday reports that Publicis is winning major accounts without formal pitches by selling AI transformation directly to chief executives.
- Brazil's Abracom and ABA have updated their pitch guidance, warning that agency hiring cannot be reduced to an automated comparison of prices and deliverables.
- A 48-hour sprint covering competitor content, audience tensions, the unclaimed angle and an evidence check can produce a category view before the first draft.
- Every insight in a pitch should trace back to real ads or posts, so it survives challenge from the client's team.

### AI-native marketing organisations: what clients still buy from agencies
URL: https://defygroup.ai/blog/ai-native-marketing-organization-agencies/
Question: My clients are building AI into their marketing teams. What does an AI-native marketing organisation actually need from an agency like mine?
Answer: An AI-native marketing organisation runs on its own data and AI layers, with a small team directing systems rather than doing tasks by hand. It needs fewer agency hours for reporting, optimisation and versioning, and more help building the system, centralising data, checking AI outputs, and supplying the creative and cultural judgement a model lacks.
Key takeaways:
- Liquid Death aims to run a sizeable media budget with only two internal people, using an AI operating system built with its agency, Power Digital Marketing.
- When a client's system optimises campaigns daily, agencies lose the hours once billed for reports, status updates and manual optimisation.
- The agency work that gains value is system design, data centralisation, checking AI outputs for accuracy, and creative and cultural judgement.
- Technology shapes what is possible but does not decide the agency's role; agencies that redesign their offer before clients ask are the ones best placed to keep the relationship.
- Independents do not need to build their own AI operating system, but they do need the capability one provides.

### AI marketing case studies with real numbers, and what they leave out
URL: https://defygroup.ai/blog/ai-driven-agency-case-studies/
Question: Where can I find AI marketing case studies with real results, so I can learn what works before I commit?
Answer: Credible AI marketing case studies are rarer than the hype suggests. The useful ones name a specific inefficiency, give a baseline, explain the method and say whether results are projected or realised. Recent examples include TRKKN's Meridian modelling for Faces, which projected an 8.5% revenue uplift, and SAMY cutting performance reporting from three days to one.
Key takeaways:
- TRKKN used Google's open-source Meridian model on three years of Faces data across 11 channels and projected an 8.5% incremental revenue lift from reallocating existing budget.
- That uplift is a modelled projection, not a realised result, and a credible case study says so plainly.
- The AI case studies worth copying fix a specific market inefficiency, such as last-click measurement or manual reporting, and report a number with a method behind it.
- Efficiency gains matter when freed time goes into better work: SAMY cut performance reporting from three days to one with Defy Agents.
- Be most sceptical of case studies that count outputs, such as assets produced, instead of business outcomes.

### AI content creation best practices: a quality framework for agencies
URL: https://defygroup.ai/blog/ai-content-quality-framework-agencies/
Question: How do I use AI to create content without losing our brand voice, creativity or effectiveness?
Answer: Treat AI output as raw material, not finished work. Write briefs that say where AI may be used and which decisions stay human, feed tools real audience evidence, edit for specificity rather than polish, pre-test concepts before media spend, record where AI shaped each asset, and judge results on business evidence instead of volume.
Key takeaways:
- AI has made polish cheap, so polish alone no longer signals quality; specificity, point of view and human detail do.
- An AI-era creative brief should state where AI can be used, which decisions stay human, how assets are reviewed and what evidence will judge the outcome.
- Quality holds when human judgement sits at fixed gates throughout the workflow, not at the end as a final read-through.
- Scoring concepts for predicted clickability before media spend catches weak work while it is still cheap to fix.
- Keeping a record of where AI shaped each asset makes disclosure manageable as transparency expectations rise in Europe.

### How AI hits each type of marketing agency: creative to influencer
URL: https://defygroup.ai/blog/how-ai-disrupts-each-agency-type/
Question: How is AI affecting different types of marketing agencies, and which AI tools should my kind of agency be looking at?
Answer: AI hits each agency type where its work is most repetitive and data-heavy: optimisation and reporting in media, production and versioning in creative, segmentation and deployment in CRM, monitoring in PR, and reporting in influencer. Because boutiques and networks now use the same tools, the advantage shifts to specialists who know things the tools do not.
Key takeaways:
- AI is the first big technology shift that does not reward agency size, because a 10-person boutique and a 1,000-person network shop can use the same platforms.
- Each agency type is disrupted where its work is most repetitive: optimisation for media, versioning for creative, deployment for CRM, monitoring for PR and reporting for influencer.
- The divide between agencies is moving from access to AI tools towards skill in using them and knowledge the tools lack.
- Promethean Research found agencies that cut services grew 13%, against 9.8% for those that expanded, so bolting on an AI department is not automatically a growth strategy.
- Specialists that partner with each other, rather than trying to own every capability, are well placed to compete with networks.

### Media consumption data in Singapore: what to trust as networks shrink
URL: https://defygroup.ai/blog/apac-agencies-market-intelligence/
Question: Where can I find accurate, reliable data on how people in Singapore consume media?
Answer: No single source gives you accurate media consumption data for Singapore. Use official statistics and regulator surveys for broad reach, audience measurement panels and platform data for exposure, and real published content for what people actually engage with and talk about. Compare them, note each one's blind spot, and treat precise averages with suspicion.
Key takeaways:
- Accurate media consumption data for Singapore comes from combining sources, because each one measures something different and misses something important.
- Surveys, platform-reported figures and measurement panels often disagree, and the disagreement is information rather than an error to average away.
- Dentsu named Singapore among the APAC markets that contracted in the first half of 2026 as it cuts overseas entities, a good moment for independents to own their market intelligence.
- Precise numbers create an illusion of understanding: an average viewing figure says nothing about why different audiences choose what they watch.
- Real published posts show what audiences actually engage with and say, and conclusions drawn from them can be checked against the source.

### AI media planning: from demographics to real consumer tensions
URL: https://defygroup.ai/blog/media-planning-real-personas-ai/
Question: How do I analyse my audience’s demographics to build media plans that actually reach the right groups?
Answer: Use demographics as a filter, not a strategy. Age, gender or income tell you who to buy, but not why that person will pay attention. With AI you can cluster your audience’s real conversations into personas and tensions, then choose channels, messages and moments from those. Demographics come last, to narrow the buy.
Key takeaways:
- Demographics answer who to buy in media; consumer tensions answer why anyone will pay attention.
- According to Reason Why, Spanish insurer Santalucía lifted spontaneous awareness from 45% to 62% in five years against rivals investing up to eight times more: understanding can outweigh spend.
- Audience data is high quality when it serves the decision in front of you, not when it merely looks more precise.
- AI earns its place in planning when it clusters real conversations into personas and tensions you can check against examples.
- A good tension-led plan still uses demographics, just at the end: to narrow the buy, not to decide the message.

### Personalised advertising without losing trust: a guide for agencies
URL: https://defygroup.ai/blog/ad-personalisation-without-third-party-data/
Question: How can brands connect better with diverse audiences, like women’s football fans, through personalised advertising?
Answer: By personalising for context and culture before tracking. Niche audiences such as women’s football fans reward brands that show they understand their world: their heroes, their language and their gripes. You get there by listening to what they post, building variants for each group and testing which creative works before you spend. Trust is the precondition, not a side effect.
Key takeaways:
- The personalisation that works today adapts to the audience’s community and moment, not to each person’s browsing history.
- Personalisation is an exchange of attention and data for relevance; if the audience feels the deal is unfair, trust breaks for the campaigns that follow as well.
- In niches such as women’s football, a single age bracket can hide very different tensions that call for different messages, tones and channels.
- SAMY’s acquisition of Get Engaged, reported by El Publicista, confirms that the market is betting on connecting through creators and culture.
- Testing creative variants before media spend turns the results conversation with the client into a conversation about evidence.

### AI for independent agencies: why they’re consolidating and what changes
URL: https://defygroup.ai/blog/independent-agency-consolidation-spain-ai/
Question: Which AI trends should my independent agency follow so we don’t fall behind the groups that are consolidating?
Answer: The trend that matters isn’t a particular tool but a shift in scale. AI shortens execution and moves value towards research, strategy and coordinating specialisms, which is why independents are joining forces. But scale no longer requires headcount alone: an agency can tap into shared intelligence without merging, if it chooses its tools well.
Key takeaways:
- AI makes execution cheaper and shifts agency value towards research, strategy and coordination between specialisms.
- According to El Publicista, Jungle Design Industries brings together four firms, 100 people and €12m in 2025 turnover to compete in strategic design.
- Technology drives consolidation but doesn’t decide it: each agency chooses whether to gain scale by merging, joining a group or relying on platforms that already exist.
- The AI trends that move margin at an independent are agents for repetitive tasks, data you can query by conversation, traceable conclusions and creative assessed before spend.
- Before you merge, measure where your team’s hours go: many agencies need tools, not size.

### AI data analysis in marketing: conclusions your clients can verify
URL: https://defygroup.ai/blog/ai-data-analysis-verifiable-conclusions/
Question: What’s best practice for analysing data with AI in marketing and making well-founded decisions?
Answer: Treat every AI conclusion as a hypothesis until you can show the data behind it. Define the question before you open the tool, bring together sources that currently live in silos, insist on traceability back to the original data and review as a team before presenting. A conclusion nobody can verify is useless for decisions, however good it sounds.
Key takeaways:
- An AI conclusion is a hypothesis until it can be traced back to the original data that supports it.
- According to Digiday, agencies are adding AI to their master service agreements clause by clause, and clients want to know which tools are used and how their data is handled.
- When clients can’t check how a conclusion was reached, they discount the value of all of them, good ones included: the classic problem of information asymmetry.
- Data silos mean AI returns partial conclusions, because it only analyses the sources it is given.
- An evidence appendix, an oversight line and a tool inventory answer in advance what clients are starting to demand.

### Social listening for agencies: why the quarterly report is already too late
URL: https://defygroup.ai/blog/continuous-social-listening-agencies/
Question: How can my agency keep up with consumer trends that change every week?
Answer: With continuous social listening, not quarterly snapshots. The agency defines which categories, competitors and conversations it tracks for each client, reviews the signals every week against agreed action thresholds and checks every conclusion against the real posts behind it. That way it spots trends while they can still be used, not once competitors have claimed them.
Key takeaways:
- A quarterly trends report describes a market that has already moved; continuous social listening turns consumer conversation into a weekly signal.
- According to Digiday, synthetic audiences are now part of everyday work at agencies and advertisers, and Aveeno Body cut the time to write a strategy brief from about 30 days to three.
- Loss aversion makes teams fear the mistake of acting more than the ground lost by not acting, even though waiting usually costs more.
- A useful listening routine sets action thresholds in advance, so every relevant signal ends in a decision rather than another slide.
- Any AI-generated conclusion should be checked against the real posts behind it before it reaches the client.

### Tariffs and marketing strategy: how to rebalance messages and budgets
URL: https://defygroup.ai/blog/tariffs-marketing-strategy-messages-budgets/
Question: How are tariffs affecting consumers, and how do I adjust my marketing strategy?
Answer: Tariffs change the structure of your category: costs rise, consumers compare more and local substitutes appear. The answer isn’t to freeze investment but to map exposure by market, listen to how the price conversation is shifting, analyse which messages competitors are moving to and rebalance message and budget country by country, with short tests.
Key takeaways:
- A tariff doesn’t just make a product dearer: it reshuffles several of the category’s five forces at once, from buyer power to the threat of substitutes.
- Freezing all investment until the picture becomes clearer amounts to planning for a market that no longer exists.
- According to Campaign, research by Publicis London, System1 and Effie concludes that global campaigns deliver fewer commercial outcomes than work designed for each market.
- The right message after a cost shock is found by analysing what the whole category is already saying and spotting which angle has been left free.
- Short tests by market take the risk out of rebalancing: scale what works and cut what doesn’t.

### Agency burnout: fewer repetitive tasks, more time for creativity
URL: https://defygroup.ai/blog/agency-burnout-automate-repetitive-work/
Question: I work at an agency and I'm constantly stressed: how do I deal with it before I burn out?
Answer: Managing agency stress starts with separating two loads: creative work, which is demanding but meaningful, and repetitive tasks such as reports, timesheets and format resizes. The second can be reduced or automated. Doing so frees up time and energy for the first and tackles one of the root causes of burnout. If the exhaustion persists, seek professional help.
Key takeaways:
- Agency burnout doesn't come only from the intensity of creative work but from the repetitive load that competes with it: reports, timesheets, resizes and status meetings.
- According to Campaign, agencies such as X&O and Beers With Friends work in short sprints with a single client, a model that puts focus ahead of fragmentation.
- Burnout theory describes three dimensions (exhaustion, cynicism and inefficacy), and mechanical work feeds all three.
- Automation only reduces stress if the time it frees up is protected for judgement-led work or rest, not filled with more load.
- If exhaustion persists or affects your health, the answer is to talk to a professional, not to rearrange your diary.

### Brand differentiation with AI: how not to sound like your competitors
URL: https://defygroup.ai/blog/brand-differentiation-ai-without-sounding-generic/
Question: How can I use AI to differentiate a brand's messaging in a crowded market without it sounding like everything else?
Answer: Use AI to map what your whole category already says, not to write the message. Analyse competitors' ads and content, identify the crowded territories and the empty ones, develop an idea of your own in that gap and test the concepts before committing media spend. AI provides the map; human judgement provides the difference.
Key takeaways:
- Used to write messages, AI drifts towards the category average; used to map what competitors say, it helps you find unclaimed territory.
- According to Marketing Week, Sir John Hegarty calls much of today's marketing "repetitive, cliché, boring" and argues that more data hasn't improved the failure rate of product launches.
- Herd behaviour pushes brands to copy their category's codes because it feels safe, even though it dilutes the return on media investment.
- A person should write the brand's point of view before AI generates a single tagline.
- A good creative filter asks two questions before any media money is spent: is the idea different, and is it likely to work?

### Agency pitches in Brazil: the new rules reward those who bring evidence

Answer: Turn up with evidence, not opinion. The updated Abracom and ABA guide calls for detailed briefs and transparent evaluation criteria, and warns that hiring an agency can't become an automated price comparison. That favours agencies that show, with real conversations and ads from the category, how consumers are changing and what the client's competitors are already doing.
Key takeaways:
- The updated Abracom and ABA guide has 10 steps and calls for detailed briefs, transparent evaluation criteria and feedback for every participating agency.
- If your proposal looks like everyone else's, the decision comes down to price, which is precisely what the guide says hiring shouldn't be.
- Consumer behaviour evidence, drawn from real conversations and content in the category, is the shortest route to beating the client's expectations in the room.
- AI speeds up the category dossier; interpretation, strategy and relationships are still people's work.

### Fragmented media consumption: understanding your audience beyond dashboards
URL: https://defygroup.ai/blog/fragmented-media-consumption-audience-data/
Question: How do I understand my audience's media consumption trends when every platform tells a different story?
Answer: Stop adding up platform reports and start with people. Gather what your audience posts, comments on and shares across every channel, cluster those conversations into personas and tensions, and only then allocate media. Fragmented data isn't fixed with more dashboards but with a common unit of analysis: the audience and what it actually says.
Key takeaways:
- In Digiday's survey of 30 agency professionals, 77% plan to increase budget for AI search and GEO in the next 12 months.
- Adding up metrics from different platforms produces a collage, not a portrait of the audience, because each network measures with its own ruler.
- Good data is data fit for purpose: consistency and completeness matter more than volume.
- Personas built from real conversations give planning a common unit across every channel.
- Comments on creators' content are among the most honest sources of what an audience really thinks.

### AI and the end of the holding company model: lessons for independent agencies
URL: https://defygroup.ai/blog/ai-holding-company-model-independent-agencies/
Question: Will AI kill the advertising holding company model? And what should my independent agency do about it?
Answer: Not overnight, but it's already changing it. Cuts at WPP and other groups show the junior-heavy pyramid giving way to lean, senior teams that orchestrate AI. For an independent agency, the advantage is having little structure and no legacy technology to pay for: you can adopt the same analytical capability without the cost of building it.
Key takeaways:
- According to the FT, as reported by The Drum, WPP is set to cut around 1,000 more roles; its headcount fell 6.4% in a year, to 97,388.
- Gartner estimates that agency fees have fallen to 19.2% of marketing budgets and forecasts 15% by 2030.
- AI is inverting the agency pyramid: fewer juniors on execution, more senior teams orchestrating systems.
- Independents, with less overhead and less legacy technology, can buy in the analytical capability the networks built in-house.
- Automate the task, not the judgement, and don't close the door on juniors.

### B2B content marketing that doesn't send decision-makers to sleep
URL: https://defygroup.ai/blog/b2b-content-marketing-that-engages/
Question: How do I make B2B content that genuinely engages and still generates qualified leads?
Answer: Swap what the brand wants to say for what the buyer feels they gain. B2B content engages when it starts from the real tensions of the people who decide (risk, timelines, budget, reputation), speaks their language and brings proof. Before investing in media, test several concepts and put money only behind those most likely to be clicked.
Key takeaways:
- Stagwell has signed the largest multi-agency deal in its history with ServiceNow, according to Adweek, a sign that B2B budgets are big and hotly contested.
- Perceived value is the sum buyers do between what they get and what they give, including time and attention.
- B2B content engages when it names the tensions of the people who decide: risk, internal politics, time and reputation.
- Scoring concepts before investing in media concentrates budget on the routes most likely to work.
- A qualified lead, defined together with sales, is the metric that closes the loop on B2B content.

### Black Friday for agencies: automate reporting, win back time to optimise
URL: https://defygroup.ai/blog/black-friday-agencies-automate-reporting/
Question: Which ecommerce strategies actually work on Black Friday, and how does my agency cope with the peak?
Answer: Decide early, automate the repetitive work and keep people free to make the calls during the peak. The Black Friday strategies that work depend on adjusting offer, creative and budget quickly, and that dies when the team spends the day building reports. Automate data collection, consolidation and alerts; keep people on budget, messaging and stock decisions with the client.
Key takeaways:
- Black Friday 2026 falls on 27 November: six weeks is enough to automate reporting, alerts and resizing, provided the work starts now.
- A study by Publicis London, System1 and Effie, reported by Campaign, indicates that global campaigns deliver fewer commercial outcomes than local ones.
- Making decisions on yesterday's report is an information failure, and at peak it costs media budget.
- Automate collection, consolidation, alerts and resizing; keep people on budget reallocation and changes to the offer.
- SAMY cut its performance reporting from three days to one with Defy Agents.

### Engagement metrics clients value (and the ones that are window dressing)
URL: https://defygroup.ai/blog/engagement-metrics-clients-value/
Question: How do I measure audience engagement in a way my client actually values, with so many different platforms?
Answer: Separate attention metrics from business metrics, then connect one to the other. Likes and reach show that something happened; saves, shares, comments with intent, branded search and incremental revenue show that it mattered. Clients value the engagement you can connect to a decision: where to invest, what to cut, what to repeat.
Key takeaways:
- Clients value the engagement metric that connects to a business decision, not the one that simply goes up.
- According to Campaign Middle East, TRKKN used Google's Meridian with three years of data across 11 channels and projected an 8.5% incremental revenue lift from reallocating budget alone.
- The data illusion effect makes a dashboard full of percentages look like understanding, even when the metric doesn't measure what matters.
- Engagement rates should only be compared within the same platform and the same format.
- Every engagement report should end with a budget recommendation.

### Agency remuneration: how to prove your value with social data
URL: https://defygroup.ai/blog/agency-remuneration-social-data-proof-of-value/
Question: How do I turn social media interactions into business insights, to the point where they justify being paid for value rather than time spent?
Answer: By turning social data into traceable proof. Buyers pay for time because it is the only thing they can verify. An agency that links each recommendation to the real posts of audiences and competitors, then to a metric agreed before the campaign, makes its value visible and can negotiate a hybrid or performance-based model.
Key takeaways:
- France's AACC is preparing a range of remuneration models, due in early December, to move agencies away from billing for time alone.
- Advertisers pay for time because it is the only value they can verify: a textbook market failure born of information asymmetry.
- To be paid for value, an agency must link every recommendation to traceable proof, from the original insight to the measured result.
- Social data shows what audiences and competitors actually publish, which makes it a more verifiable evidence base than a self-reported survey.
- The level of proof an agency can produce determines the remuneration model it can negotiate.

### Media agencies and AI: what the new era means for independents
URL: https://defygroup.ai/blog/media-agencies-new-ai-era-independents/
Question: How is AI changing the media agency business, and which tools should an independent agency adopt to stay in the race?
Answer: AI absorbs execution first: reporting, data consolidation, repetitive optimisation. A media agency's value moves up towards advice, understanding the client's business and the ability to challenge a brief. For an independent, the point is not to pile up tools but to get the same depth of analysis as the big groups without bearing the cost of building it.
Key takeaways:
- According to Stratégies, AI will compress part of media agencies' execution and shift their value towards advice and understanding the client's business.
- Each type of agency is hit differently, but everywhere AI first removes the work the client never saw.
- Technology forces execution to compress; it doesn't decide what the agency does with the time freed up.
- For an independent, the challenge is to reach the same depth of analysis as the big groups without building or maintaining its own tech stack.
- An agency that claims a strategic role can no longer bill mainly for time spent.

### Research without respondents: are synthetic personas promise or mirage?
URL: https://defygroup.ai/blog/respondent-free-research-synthetic-personas/
Question: Can I trust synthetic personas to understand Gen Z or older consumers, or do I still need real respondents?
Answer: For exploring, yes; for concluding, no. Synthetic personas test scenarios and messages quickly, but they play back what the model has learned, generational clichés included, and claim no representativeness. For generational research, anchor every conclusion in real observed behaviour, such as the content these audiences actually publish, then use synthetic personas to test.
Key takeaways:
- Respondent-free research platforms, such as Limpid, launched by Patrick van Bloeme, let you run a qualitative study on synthetic personas in a few hours, without claiming statistical representativeness.
- The main risk is the data illusion effect: a fluent, precise answer inspires confidence even when it rests on no real behaviour.
- Generational research is particularly exposed, because a model learns the clichés about a generation as much as its behaviour.
- Good practice is to anchor insights in content that has actually been published, then use synthetic personas to explore and test.
- Every recommendation should state what comes from synthetic, observed and self-reported sources.

### Imposter syndrome in agencies: rebuilding confidence in the AI era
URL: https://defygroup.ai/blog/imposter-syndrome-agencies-ai-era/
Question: What if my work isn't good enough? How do I deal with imposter syndrome in an agency, now that AI does part of my job?
Answer: Imposter syndrome thrives in agencies because work is judged constantly and rarely measured. AI makes it worse when you treat it as a rival, and eases it when it becomes a support. The most solid remedy: back your ideas with verifiable evidence, ask early and, for leaders, redesign junior roles rather than cut them.
Key takeaways:
- Imposter syndrome thrives in agencies because work is judged constantly, against criteria that change from one brief to the next.
- AI adds a new kind of doubt, especially for juniors, whose learning tasks are exactly the ones it absorbs.
- According to one participant quoted by Digiday, the drop in junior hiring is a training challenge, not a technology one: those roles need redesigning, not cutting.
- Confidence built on verifiable evidence stands up to client questions better than confidence built on bravado.
- Agency leaders reduce the phenomenon by making questions normal and pairing seniors with juniors.

### Measuring cross-platform engagement: time to retire the agency spreadsheet
URL: https://defygroup.ai/blog/measure-cross-platform-engagement-agencies/
Question: Which tools can reliably measure my audience's engagement across every platform, when each one counts it differently?
Answer: No single tool does it alone, because every platform defines engagement differently. The reliable method: agree one shared definition of engagement, normalise metrics platform by platform, centralise the data in a single analysis layer and link the numbers to the conversations that explain them. Do that, and the hand-stitched spreadsheet becomes redundant.
Key takeaways:
- No single tool can reliably measure cross-platform engagement on its own, because each platform defines and counts engagement in its own way.
- According to Campaign UK, the Ingenuity Pulse report finds that only one in three marketers is satisfied with their martech investments – a gap that puts the client-agency relationship at risk.
- Stacking specialist tools does not create an overall view: a system's value depends on the connections between its parts.
- Consistent measurement rests on a shared definition, metrics normalised by platform, a competitive benchmark and conversations that explain the numbers.
- With sports content, much of the engagement happens away from the official accounts, around the big moments.

### Narrowing your agency's service offering: what to stop, and when
URL: https://defygroup.ai/blog/when-to-stop-an-agency-service/
Question: How do I know which service my agency should stop selling, and what data should I base the decision on?
Answer: Stop a service when it is no longer differentiating, profitable or backed by the market you are targeting. The data usually tells you before the P&L does: clients bringing work in-house, cheaper competitors, formats declining in the category. According to Promethean Research, cited by Campaign US, agencies that narrowed their offer grew 13%, against 9.8% for those that expanded it.
Key takeaways:
- According to Promethean Research, cited by Campaign US, agencies that cut services grew 13%, versus 9.8% for those that expanded their offer and 5.7% for those that changed nothing.
- The three most common triggers are clients taking work in-house, the service becoming a commodity and the agency spreading itself too thin.
- According to expectation confirmation theory, a half-delivered service disappoints and weakens the whole client relationship, not just that one service.
- A single client request is not a market: the decision should rest on category demand, real profitability and operational capacity.
- The signs that a service has had its day show up in market data long before they appear in the P&L.

### Agency pricing models for AI: price it fairly, don't give away your margin
URL: https://defygroup.ai/blog/agency-pricing-models-fair-ai-pricing/
Question: How do I bill for AI work in my agency without the efficiency gains eating into my margin?
Answer: Separate two things: the cost of the AI and the value of the output. Show licences and compute transparently, as a line item or a credit allowance, and price strategy, creative and media planning on outcomes rather than hours. Pass every efficiency gain on through lower fees and you make your work interchangeable – and therefore price-sensitive.
Key takeaways:
- AI cuts the time a job takes, but not automatically the cost: licences, compute and quality assurance belong in the calculation.
- Agencies that pass AI efficiency on in full through lower hourly fees are penalising themselves for being productive.
- The more interchangeable a service looks, the more price-elastic clients become – judgement, category knowledge and relationships are what keep fees stable.
- For most independent agencies, a hybrid of a transparent AI line item, fixed-fee routine work and value-based strategy is the most pragmatic route.

### AI tools for agencies: how MCP gets you out of the tool sprawl
URL: https://defygroup.ai/blog/ai-tools-agencies-mcp-integration/
Question: Which AI tools should my agency use – and how do I integrate them without ending up in tool chaos?
Answer: Don't start with the tool; start with the workflows that eat the most time. Choose one central workspace, such as an AI assistant like Claude, and connect your data through open interfaces such as the Model Context Protocol (MCP) rather than adding a new dashboard for every task. What matters is integration, traceability and clear sign-off rules.
Key takeaways:
- More AI tools don't mean more output: without integration you get data silos, duplicated work and knowledge that lives with individual people.
- The Model Context Protocol (MCP) is an open standard that lets AI assistants access data sources and tools directly – without yet another dashboard.
- The big agency groups are selling their AI agents on governance and human accountability; independent agencies should spell out control just as clearly.
- The right order is: workflow, data source, interface, rules – and only then the tool.

Set a baseline in October, agree thresholds with the client and get alternative messages signed off before Black Friday on 27 November.
Key takeaways:
- At Christmas, waiting is the most expensive option, because bad decisions only become visible once the budget has been spent.
- Social listening provides early indicators such as price sensitivity, gift uncertainty and competitor promotions, long before they show up in sales data.
- According to research by Publicis London, System1 and Effie reported by Campaign UK, global campaigns deliver fewer commercial outcomes than work for local markets.
